subject.title: fix(scheduler): absorb bot sync timestamp lag

question: Should scheduler reconciliation use an event/actor-aware signal for bot writes, rather than suppressing every `updated_at` value in a five-second timestamp window?
rationale: Timestamp comparison alone cannot distinguish the delayed bot write from a genuine human action in the same interval, so the acceptable accuracy-versus-complexity boundary needs an explicit maintainer choice.

options.title: Use event-aware reconciliation
options.body: Record or query a bot-identifiable event signal so delayed bot writes can be ignored without discarding nearby human activity.

options.title: Accept bounded suppression
options.body: Keep the timestamp-only window but explicitly accept that human activity inside five seconds can be missed until later activity occurs.

options.title: Defer the change
options.body: Leave the current behavior in place until the scheduler has enough event provenance to make the distinction safely.

recommendation.title: Use event-aware reconciliation
recommendation.body: Record or query a bot-identifiable event signal so delayed bot writes can be ignored without discarding nearby human activity.
